data.title: Target of rapamycin and regulation of membrane transporters: integrating nutrient sensing, stress adaptation and lifespan across eukaryotes
data.authors: Xintarakou O; Twardowska NP; Rallis C

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Narrative review arguing that membrane transporters are part of the TOR network rather than only nutrient suppliers, with TOR in turn controlling their activity, trafficking and degradation. Evidence is clearest in budding and fission yeast and less tested in metazoans; the authors present TOR-transporter coupling as an untested framework for stress resistance and lifespan, not a settled conclusion.
data.abstract_excerpt: Nutrient availability is typically treated as an input to the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, the conserved controller of growth, metabolism and ageing. Yet, membrane transporters are not merely suppliers of the amino acids and other nutrients that activate TOR, they are integral components of the signalling network itself, and TOR in turn governs their activity, abundance, trafficking and degradation.
